slides: Let's continue with the pictures of similar triangles on the exam.

slides.say: Now, how do similar triangles usually show up on the exam? They come in three pictures. Let's start with the first one, a line parallel to the base.
Here's a triangle, A B C. Inside it we draw D E, parallel to the base, B C.
The lines are parallel, so the angle at D is equal to the angle at B. These are corresponding angles, like we learned with parallel lines. In the same way, the angle at E is equal to the angle at C.
at: the angle at D is equal

slides.say: So the small triangle, A D E, and the big triangle, A B C, have the same angles. They're similar.

slides: This picture is a bit confusing, and here's why. Let's match the sides by the angles.

slides.say: D E sits opposite the angle at A, in the small triangle. In the big one, B C sits opposite that angle. So D E matches B C.
Now A E. A common mistake is to say that A E matches E C. But E C isn't a side of either triangle. It's a side of the trapezoid at the bottom.
A E is opposite alpha, the angle at D, in the small triangle. Opposite alpha in the big triangle, the angle at B, is the whole side, A C. So A E matches the whole A C.
at: So A E matches the whole

slides.say: In the same way, A D is opposite beta, so it matches the whole side, A B. Always check which angle a side is opposite.
at: so it matches the whole side

slides.say: There's one more rule here. It's only about the two sides, A B and A C.
A line parallel to the base cuts these two sides in the same ratio. So A D to D B is equal to A E to E C. That's the part to part rule.
at: So A D to D B

slides.say: Here A D is three and D B is two. A E is six and E C is four. Three over two is one and a half, and six over four is also one and a half.
So why did we say that A E doesn't match E C? Because of D E. D E isn't a part of a side. It matches the whole B C.
A B is three plus two, five. So D E to B C is three to five, like A D to the whole A B. It's not three to two.
at: A B is three plus two
So D E to B C is three to five

slides: So for the parts of the two sides, part to part is fine. But the parallel line itself always goes with the whole side. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next part.
